results.text: Management of Severe Bisoprolol Poisoning Using Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy: A Case Report and Literature Review. We report the case of a 65-year-old Caucasian woman who presented to our emergency department following the ingestion of approximately thirty 2.5 mg bisoprolol tablets. Initially stable, she rapidly developed severe bradycardia and hypotension, culminating in cardiogenic-distributive shock that required intubation, aggressive vasoactive support, and advanced metabolic therapies. results.text: Cardiac arrest due to airway obstruction in Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor-induced angioedema. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor-induced angioedema is a rare but serious side effect of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi). It causes bradykinin accumulation, leading to the swelling of various tissus, including upper airway.
